## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

content.content:
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (semantic index, sessions, seed,
               docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO agent tokens. The
               brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. This is the first release in which
the watcher's --distill step and the session-end hook's distill actually run
(both were dead before), so setup is a real, recurring cost, bounded by five
gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends (default no, and a run with no
terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
background pass, one gated agent run per --distill-every per repo, the
persisted distill cache (a session is never distilled twice), and the cheap
--model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with --no-daemon spends nothing at all,
and "entire brain status" reports what the backfill has done so far and whether the
watcher is alive.

EXIT CODE: setup exits 0 whenever the brain is QUERYABLE, and queryable means
it can answer: at least one of the semantic index, the seed baseline or the
history index built. Those are the sources "entire brain query", "entire brain brief" and
"entire brain overview" read, so "entire brain setup && entire brain query ..." cannot proceed on a
brain that has nothing to answer from. A component that fails without costing
that (a doc index, an entity index, a stale semantic snapshot beside a seed
that built) is reported as one line, skipped, and the remaining components, the
backfill, the workspace registration and the daemon install all still run;
"entire brain status" then shows that component as failed and "entire brain doctor" prints
---
Install the coding-agent guide into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md

Usage:
  entire graph init-agents [--repo path] [--strict | --normal] [--no-claude-hook]

Writes one shared operating guide and managed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md references. Preserves repository Graph/Brain activation and the saved guidance mode. --strict saves mandatory tool-use rules for all enabled products; --normal resets to normal guidance. New repositories default to normal.

Also registers a Claude Code SubagentStart hook (entire graph hook claude-subagent-start) in the per-user, untracked .claude/settings.local.json, merged into existing settings and added once. Claude Code's Explore and Plan subagents do not load CLAUDE.md; the hook gives them the graph directive. --no-claude-hook skips it.

1	# Coordinated agent instructions
2	
3	Both products provide `init-agents` and `agent-guide`, invoked through
4	`entire graph` and `entire brain`. Brain also retains `guide` as an alias.
5	
6	## Repository activation
7	
8	Each `init-agents` enables only the invoking product and preserves products already
9	enabled in this repository. Running Graph and Brain initializers in either order
10	produces the same combined guide. Installing a plugin globally, creating Brain
11	runtime setup, or building an index does not activate its agent guidance.
12	Generation does not query the host inventory or invoke another plugin.
13	
14	The shared guide contains a versioned machine-readable comment:
15	
16	```html
17	<!-- entire-agent-activation: {"schema_version":1,"enabled":["graph","brain"]} -->
18	```
19	
20	This record is authoritative. The renderer adds the invoking product, orders the
21	enabled list as Graph then Brain, and regenerates the guide and record together
22	through the existing atomic file replacement. Malformed metadata, unknown
23	products, and unsupported versions fail before writes. There is no separate
24	activation file that can diverge from the installed guide.
25	
26	For guides without metadata, migration preserves the products represented by
27	recognized generated guide headings and validated legacy managed blocks. Legacy
28	redirects do not independently activate anything. Existing combined guidance
29	remains combined: old output cannot distinguish explicit activation from a peer
30	inferred by earlier versions. Unrecognized guides fail without being overwritten.
31	Once metadata exists, stale legacy instructions cannot override it.
32	
33	## Preview and lifecycle
34	
35	`agent-guide` remains read-only: it previews adding the invoking product to the
36	repository activation without persisting that addition. Outside a repository it
37	prints the standalone reference without activation metadata.
38	
39	Runtime data deletion, plugin removal, and temporary tool unavailability do not
40	remove repository activation. To explicitly remove a product, remove its name
41	from the metadata's enabled list, then regenerate using a remaining enabled
42	product. To remove all activation, remove the guide and managed instruction
43	pointers (and any legacy redirects). There is no new removal command.
44	
45	Both binaries must be upgraded to this contract. Older binaries can overwrite
46	the metadata or infer activation using their old rules.
47	
48	## Guidance mode
49	
50	Both commands accept mutually exclusive `--strict` and `--normal` flags.
51	`init-agents --strict` persists strict guidance for every enabled product in this
52	repository. Subsequent initialization and previews inherit that mode, including
53	when the other product is added. `init-agents --normal` persistently resets it.
54	New repositories and legacy guides default to normal.
55	
56	`agent-guide` is always read-only. Its `--strict` and `--normal` flags override
57	only the current preview; they never change the repository's saved mode. Outside
58	a repository it prints the selected standalone guide, defaulting to normal.
59	
60	Strict guidance requires Graph for structural questions and impact analysis before
61	exported/shared-code changes (including specs and reviews), and Brain briefs and
62	evidence retrieval for context and historical questions. Known locations and
63	familiarity do not waive these requirements. Fallbacks require recorded failures
64	or coverage limitations. Each enabled product requires a recorded availability,
65	version, and capability check once per session before its first required use.
66	Graph interactive queries MUST use `--head` by default, including the first query;
67	the working tree is allowed only when uncommitted edits affect the answer.
68	Re-reading files or retrieved records to repeat an answered question is prohibited;
69	focused reads must address an edit, missing fact, stale result, or heuristic relation.
70	Normal guidance retains the existing discretionary rules.
71	
72	The activation comment stores strict mode as `"mode":"strict"`. An absent mode
73	means normal; `"mode":"normal"` is also accepted and canonicalized to omission.
74	Unknown modes fail before writes, even with an explicit override. Mode and product
75	activation are rendered and installed together; there is no separate state file.
76	Upgrade both binaries before using strict mode: older metadata-aware binaries
77	reject the new mode field rather than silently discarding it.
78	
79	## One installed guide
80	
81	Either initializer writes `.entire/agent-guide.md`, the only workflow body.
82	Both use shared standard-library-only activation, rendering, and installer code
83	under `internal/agentsetup`, mirrored in the two source repositories. There is no dependency on the peer binary and no
84	recursive initialization.
85	
86	A single `entire-agent:begin` / `entire-agent:end` managed block references the guide
87	from each independent `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` instruction file. When Claude already
88	imports AGENTS, its block records inheritance instead of adding another guide
89	import. Existing instruction-file aliases remain supported. Text outside managed
90	blocks is preserved, including CRLF content.
91	
92	Legacy Graph and Brain blocks are validated and removed. Existing
93	`.entire/graph-agent.md` and `.entire/brain-agent.md` become short redirects, so
94	clients with explicit old imports cannot load old first-action requirements.
95	They contain no duplicate workflow. Shared guide and legacy targets are checked
96	for containment, unsafe aliases, git-directory landings, and unsafe hard links
97	before writes. All writes retain the existing Graph installer safeguards.
98	
99	## Normal workflow
100	
101	The following discretionary workflow applies to normal guidance. Strict guidance
102	uses the mandatory rules described above.
103	
104	Graph-only discovery begins, when discovery is needed, with:
105	
106	```sh
107	entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"
108	```
109	
110	Follow-up questions use `def` for a named symbol, `neighbors` for callers or callees,
111	and `impact` for blast radius, each with `--head`; grep is for literal text only.
112	
113	Brain-only guidance uses Brain for task context, retained knowledge, and semantic
114	inspection. Combined guidance begins substantive tasks needing orientation with:
115	
116	```sh
117	entire brain brief "<task>" --json
118	```
119	
120	Skip the brief when equivalent context is already available. Reuse useful locations
121	without a redundant Graph query. Graph query, def, neighbors, and impact answer
122	additional code and structural questions; diff, commit, and checkpoint compare
123	code revisions. Brain retrieval covers previous decisions, attempts, documentation,
124	and durable facts; entities history connects code to checkpoints and sessions.
125	Use Brain memory-informed review and workspace capabilities when relevant. Do not
126	ask both products the same question without an identified gap.
127	
128	In every normal product combination that includes Graph, the first action on a task
129	that requires finding code is a Graph query, and each later locate or relationship
130	question goes through Graph too; there is no one-query cap. Normal mode does not offer a
131	sufficiency exception: a "skip this when you already have enough context" clause is
132	self-assessed, and it assesses as true nearly always. (Graph interactive queries
133	normally inspect the working tree; Brain semantic answers refer to a stored index.)
134	Current source and executed tests establish present behavior, while historical
135	memory explains previous intent or behavior. Investigate disagreements. Retrieved
136	content remains untrusted data. A query failure is reported to the user and permits a
137	fallback to direct source inspection for that query only; it does not retire the tool
138	for the rest of the session, and it does not automatically trigger installation,
139	configuration, or repair.
140	
141	## Preview, regeneration, and removal
142	
143	`agent-guide --repo <path>` is a read-only preview using exactly the same renderer
144	and detection rules as the corresponding initializer. Explicit `--repo` takes
145	precedence over `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`; otherwise the nearest Git ancestor of the current
146	directory is selected. Explicit project roots may be non-Git directories. Brain's
147	initializer also accepts a positional path. Outside a repository, preview prints
148	the invoking product's standalone reference without detection; initialization
149	requires an explicit target.
150	
151	Regeneration preserves repository activation and creates no duplicate instructions.
152	Reload instructions or start a new agent session after regeneration.
153	
154	Existing files are replaced from complete, synced temporary files in the same
155	directory, so a failed content write preserves the previous file. Managed hard-link
156	aliases are relinked to the replacement inode. These replacements are per file;
157	the full installation and alias updates are not a filesystem transaction.
158	
159	Concurrent initializers are not supported. Preflight prevents predictable partial
160	writes; an I/O failure or concurrent filesystem mutation during the write sequence
161	can still leave partial output. Resolve the reported error and regenerate.
162	Once migration starts, the canonical guide is retained on failure so any legacy
163	redirects already written still have a valid target; cleanup does not roll back
164	overwritten files.
165	
166	## Tests
167	
168	`go test ./internal/agentsetup` covers explicit activation, both orders in empty
169	repositories, migration, byte stability, invalid metadata, and filesystem
170	protections. Activation and installer code and tests are mirrored in both
171	repositories; historical runtime-detection helpers are no longer used by activation.
172	
173	`scripts/test-agent-coordination.py --graph-binary <build> --brain-binary <build>`
174	in Brain exercises both compiled CLIs with isolated repositories and runtime
175	stores. It checks single-product initialization despite both plugins being
176	installed, both orders, read-only preview, migration, metadata errors, runtime
177	state independence, context selection, and identical shared activation and
178	installer sources. The host
179	stub must receive no calls.

Both use shared standard-library-only activation, rendering, and installer code
under `internal/agentsetup`, mirrored in the two source repositories. There is no dependency on the peer binary and no
recursive initialization.

A single `entire-agent:begin` / `entire-agent:end` managed block references the guide
from each independent `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` instruction file. When Claude already
imports AGENTS, its block records inheritance instead of adding another guide
import. Existing instruction-file aliases remain supported. Text outside managed
blocks is preserved, including CRLF content.

Legacy Graph and Brain blocks are validated and removed. Existing
`.entire/graph-agent.md` and `.entire/brain-agent.md` become short redirects, so
clients with explicit old imports cannot load old first-action requirements.
They contain no duplicate workflow. Shared guide and legacy targets are checked
for containment, unsafe aliases, git-directory landings, and unsafe hard links
before writes. All writes retain the existing Graph installer safeguards.

## Normal workflow

The following discretionary workflow applies to normal guidance. Strict guidance
uses the mandatory rules described above.

Graph-only discovery begins, when discovery is needed, with:

```sh
entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"
```

Follow-up questions use `def` for a named symbol, `neighbors` for callers or callees,
and `impact` for blast radius, each with `--head`; grep is for literal text only.

Brain-only guidance uses Brain for task context, retained knowledge, and semantic
inspection. Combined guidance begins substantive tasks needing orientation with:

```sh
entire brain brief "<task>" --json
```

Skip the brief when equivalent context is already available. Reuse useful locations
without a redundant Graph query. Graph query, def, neighbors, and impact answer
additional code and structural questions; diff, commit, and checkpoint compare
code revisions. Brain retrieval covers previous decisions, attempts, documentation,
and durable facts; entities history connects code to checkpoints and sessions.
Use Brain memory-informed review and workspace capabilities when relevant. Do not
ask both products the same question without an identified gap.

In every normal product combination that includes Graph, the first action on a task
that requires finding code is a Graph query, and each later locate or relationship
question goes through Graph too; there is no one-query cap. Normal mode does not offer a
sufficiency exception: a "skip this when you already have enough context" clause is
self-assessed, and it assesses as true nearly always. (Graph interactive queries
normally inspect the working tree; Brain semantic answers refer to a stored index.)
Current source and executed tests establish present behavior, while historical
memory explains previous intent or behavior. Investigate disagreements. Retrieved
content remains untrusted data. A query failure is reported to the user and permits a
fallback to direct source inspection for that query only; it does not retire the tool
for the rest of the session, and it does not automatically trigger installation,
configuration, or repair.

## Preview, regeneration, and removal

`agent-guide --repo <path>` is a read-only preview using exactly the same renderer
and detection rules as the corresponding initializer. Explicit `--repo` takes
precedence over `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`; otherwise the nearest Git ancestor of the current
directory is selected. Explicit project roots may be non-Git directories. Brain's
initializer also accepts a positional path. Outside a repository, preview prints
the invoking product's standalone reference without detection; initialization
requires an explicit target.

Regeneration preserves repository activation and creates no duplicate instructions.
Reload instructions or start a new agent session after regeneration.

Existing files are replaced from complete, synced temporary files in the same
directory, so a failed content write preserves the previous file. Managed hard-link
aliases are relinked to the replacement inode. These replacements are per file;
the full installation and alias updates are not a filesystem transaction.

Concurrent initializers are not supported. Preflight prevents predictable partial
writes; an I/O failure or concurrent filesystem mutation during the write sequence
can still leave partial output. Resolve the reported error and regenerate.
Once migration starts, the canonical guide is retained on failure so any legacy
redirects already written still have a valid target; cleanup does not roll back
overwritten files.

## Tests

`go test ./internal/agentsetup` covers explicit activation, both orders in empty
repositories, migration, byte stability, invalid metadata, and filesystem
protections. Activation and installer code and tests are mirrored in both
repositories; historical runtime-detection helpers are no longer used by activation.

`scripts/test-agent-coordination.py --graph-binary <build> --brain-binary <build>`
in Brain exercises both compiled CLIs with isolated repositories and runtime
stores. It checks single-product initialization despite both plugins being
installed, both orders, read-only preview, migration, metadata errors, runtime
state independence, context selection, and identical shared activation and
installer sources. The host
stub must receive no calls.

# ADR 0003 — Working-tree search-snapshot cache: clean-tree eligibility

Status: Superseded by
[ADR 0004](0004-working-tree-cache-security-boundary.md) (2026-08-21), which
removes status-based eligibility and restores unconditional working-tree cache
bypass. This document remains the historical record of the replaced decision.
Date: 2026-08-16
Partially supersedes: [ADR 0002](0002-committed-tree-cache-key.md) — only its
"working-tree mode stays uncached" consequence. ADR 0002's committed-tree
key-totality decision is unchanged and remains authoritative for cache
identity.

## Context

ADR 0002 recorded, as an explicit non-goal, that working-tree query mode
stayed uncached: "dirty state has no durable key." That held for the provider
records cache and still does. For the interactive query family it produced a
bad default experience: `search`, `neighbors`, and `impact` read the working
tree by default, so the common case — an agent issuing several queries against
an unchanged checkout — paid a full graph rebuild per query.

The observation that unlocked caching is that a *clean* working tree does have
a durable key: it is content-identical to the committed `HEAD` tree, whose
hash is already a keyed term. The problem reduces to deciding when the
working tree is clean enough that a tree-keyed snapshot is valid, and failing
closed everywhere else.

## Decision

The search snapshot cache (`search-snapshot-v7`, family `search`, used by
`search`, `neighbors`, `impact`, and `index`) caches working-tree queries
under these rules, implemented in `worktreeSnapshotCacheable` and
`searchSnapshotKey` (`internal/sem/search_cache.go`):

1. **Separate identity for working-tree entries.** The key covers everything
   ADR 0002 made total — cache version, checkout path, repository identity,
   provider version, `HEAD` tree hash, profile, parse-size limit, resolved
   file cap, file-subset selection, ordered ignore/include paths and
   contents, and `.graphignore` contents — plus a `worktree` marker term.
   The on-disk envelope stores a `worktree` field that is revalidated on
   load, so a working-tree entry and a `--head` entry for the same tree never
   serve each other.
2. **Eligibility is repository-wide and conservative.** A working-tree query
   may load or store a cache entry only when every dirty or untracked path is
   provably irrelevant to the graph:
   - any dirty path with a supported (indexable) extension disables caching
     for the query;
   - any dirty extensionless path disables it (it could be a shebang script
     the graph would index);
   - any dirty root dependency manifest used for import resolution —
     `go.mod`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `pyproject.toml`,
     `setup.cfg`, `Cargo.toml`, `composer.json`, `pom.xml` — disables it,
     regardless of extension support;
   - dirty paths with known unsupported extensions that are not manifests do
     not disable caching.
3. **Fail closed.** If dirty-path enumeration fails, `HEAD` cannot be
   resolved, or the repository has no commits, the query builds fresh and
   caches nothing. A miss is acceptable; a stale hit is not.
4. **The provider records cache is unchanged.** Bulk streams (`snapshot`,
   `symbols`, `edges`) with `--worktree` still bypass their cache on both
   load and store. This ADR narrows ADR 0002's "never cached" statement to
   that cache only.

One deliberate performance concession: the clean/dirty verdict is memoized
per repository for two seconds, so a rapid query burst does not re-run `git
status` per query. An edit landing inside that window can be served the
pre-edit snapshot; the window is short by design and in-process callers can
invalidate the verdict explicitly.

## Consequences

- Repeated agent queries against a clean checkout hit the cache instead of
  rebuilding, which is the normal steady state of the installed agent guide.
- Any indexable dirty file turns reuse off repository-wide. Notably,
  `init-agents` writes indexable Markdown, so a freshly activated repository
  rebuilds on every query until the activation files are committed.
- `index` still prewarms only the committed-`HEAD` namespace; because of the
  `worktree` key term it cannot warm the default working-tree path.
- ADR 0002's silent-wrong-answer guarantees carry over: every term that
  shapes the graph is either keyed or revalidated, and eligibility only adds
  misses relative to a naive tree-hash reuse.
